summary: The root لذذ primarily means to be sweet, delicious, or pleasant. It refers to something that is agreeable to the taste or senses, causing enjoyment and delight.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: لَ َّ, (T, M, L, Msb, K,) second per. لَ ِ ْتَ, (Msb,) aor. يَلَ ُّ, (T, Msb,) inf. n. لَ َا َةٌ (A, L, Msb) and لَ َا ٌ (Msb) and لَ َّةٌ; (A;) and, inf. n. إِلْتِ ا ٌ; (A;) It (a thing) was, or became لَ ِي [i. e. pleasant, delightful, delicious, luscious, sweet, or savoury; see لَ َّةٌ, below; and see طَابَ ]; (T, M, L, Msb, K;) an object of desire, or a thing desired. (L.) لَ َّهُ, (M, L, K,) first pers. لَ ِ ْتُ, (T, S, Msb,) aor. يَلَ ُّ, (T, M, L, Msb,) inf. n.

لا ّ الرَّجُلُ ٱمْرَأَتَهُ, inf. n. مُلَا َّةٌ and لِ َا ٌ, [ The man gave pleasure, or delight, or enjoyment, to his wife, receiving the same from her, ] on the occasion of contact in the act of concubitus. (A.) See also 6.
تَلَ َّ ْتُ [ I became pleased, or delighted; or I pleased, or delighted, myself ]. (A.) See also 1.
تَلَا َّا [ They (a husband and his wife) gave each other pleasure, or delight, or enjoyment, ] on the occasion of contact in the act of concubitus. (A.) See also 3.
إِسْتَلْ َ َ see 1. [ استل ّ also signifies He experienced pleasure, or delight. ]
لَ ٌّ Sleep. (IAar, T, S, L, K.) See also لَ َّةٌ and لَ ِيدٌ.

لَ َّةٌ Pleasure; delight; contr. of أَلَمٌ; (M, L, K;) so explained because it happens not save to one who is of sound constitution, free from pains; syn. with شَهْوَةٌ [in one of the senses of this latter word], or nearly so: (TA:) pleasantness; delightfulness; deliciousness; lusciousness, sweetness: (the Lexicons passim: see the intrans. v. لَ َّ, of which it is an inf. n.) pl. لَ َّاتٌ.

لَ ِي ٌ and are used in the same manner, as epithets, (Lth, T, L,) from the intrans. v. لَ َّ, (L,) signifying Pleasant, delightful, delicious, luscious, sweet, or savoury; (the Lexicons passim;) desirable, or desired: (L:) pl. of both, لِ َا ٌ; and of the latter, [or of both,] لُ ٌّ.
َا أَطْيَبُ وَأَلَ ُّ [ This is more. or most. pleasant and delightful, &c.] (A.)

مَلَ ٌّ A place of لَ َّة [i. e. pleasure, or delight ]: pl. مَلَا ُّ. It is said in a trad. إِ َا رَكِبَ أَحَدُكُمُ الدَّابَّةَ فَلْيَحْمِلْهَا عَلَى مَلَا ِّهَا [ When any one of you rides the beast of carriage, let him urge it to run upon the places that are pleasant to it ]; i. e. let him make it run upon plain, or even, not rugged, ground, (L.)

اَللَّ ْ and اَللَّ ِ [thus written with two láms] dial. forms of الَّ ِى: dual اللَّ َا, with the ن elided: pl. الَّ ِينَ; and sometimes, in the nom. case, الَّ ُونَ. (S.) Their proper art. is ل ى. (IB, K.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce تَزَبَّى.]

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
